human_tolerance.notes: In Sweden magpies are exclusively associated with human settlements and are rarely found more than a few hundred metres from a dwelling; they breed at high densities in suburban parks and gardens and are frequently seen close to city centres.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Courtship display (head-feather raising, tail fanning, soft calling, short buoyant chase flights) precedes egg-laying in spring.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Clutches (usually 5-6 eggs) are typically laid in April in Europe; incubation 21-22 days, fledging at around 27 days, with several further weeks of parental care. Only a single brood is reared unless the first clutch is lost.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Pairs are monogamous and generally occupy the same territory across successive years; magpies are usually sedentary.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Non-breeding birds and those not yet paired gather in flocks and roost communally in winter evenings, sometimes alongside starlings, thrushes, pigeons and jackdaws.

vocalizations.description: A choking chatter 'chac-chac' or repetitive 'chac-chac-chac-chac', used year-round as both contact call and alarm; also functions as the species' distinctive rattling call from a perch.
Young magpies make an acute 'uik uik' call resembling the barking of a small dog while begging for food; both adults and young can also produce a barely audible hiss.

external.note: iNaturalist, NCBI and eBird ids via Wikidata (P3151, P685, P3444); the iNaturalist search API also matched taxon 891696 directly to 'Eurasian Magpie'.

conservation.note: Wikipedia: 'the species is classified by the International Union for Conservation of Nature as being of Least Concern.'

range.note: Country list derived from the Distribution and habitat section ('extends across temperate Eurasia from Portugal, Spain and Ireland in the west to the Kamchatka Peninsula in the east') plus the subspecies list in Taxonomy (British Isles, Scandinavia, Russia, Mediterranean, Caucasus, Iraq, Iran, Central Asia, Pakistan, Siberia, China, Kamchatka); only countries with reasonably clear coverage were listed, so this is an approximation of the full range, not an exhaustive one. No introduced range was found.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Judgement: corvids walk and hop on the ground and fly; not explicitly itemised in the source text, inferred from the family and the 'Short, buoyant flights' courtship description.

traits.nest_type.note: Judgement mapping: the source describes a large stick-and-clay structure with a domed roof and single entrance built in a tree fork ('a stout, though loosely built, dome of prickly branches with a single, well-concealed entrance'); the schema's enum (Cup/Cavity/Platform/Ground/Burrow/None) has no domed-stick-nest option, so 'Platform' was chosen as the closest fit.

traits.perching.note: Prefers tall trees for nesting and is a corvid/passerine perching bird.

traits.size_class.note: From mass_kg (~0.22 kg); the validator's size-class bands place this in the Small band despite the magpie's long tail making it look larger.

traits.mass_kg.note: Mean of the male range midpoint (210-272 g -> 241 g) and female range midpoint (182-214 g -> 198 g) = 219.5 g, for the nominate subspecies P. p. pica. (Wikidata P2067 also carries a 9.9 g quantity, but that value is qualified 'of' an egg-weight record elsewhere in the same article, not body mass, so it was not used.)

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Full span across sexes: males 210-272 g, females 182-214 g.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of 44-46 cm (adult male, nominate subspecies; 'more than half of which is the tail').

traits.wingspan_m.note: Wikidata Q25307 wingspan (P2050): 56 cm; consistent with Wikipedia's 52-62 cm range.

traits.lifespan_y.note: From a Sheffield ringing study: '69% [annual adult survival], implying that for those birds that survive the first year, the average total lifespan was 3.7 years.' The source separately notes a maximum recorded age of 21 years 8 months.

traits.diet.note: Judgement: no sourced percentages were found. Wikipedia's Feeding section only lists diet items qualitatively ('omnivorous, eating young birds and eggs, small mammals, insects, scraps and carrion, acorns, grain, and other vegetable substances'); shares were authored to reflect that ordering (invertebrates and small vertebrates/eggs as the largest components, carrion and mast/seed smaller).

traits.social.note: 'They are monogamous, and the pairs often remain together from one breeding season to the next.' Non-breeders and juveniles form flocks (see seasonal.phases), but the breeding social unit is a pair.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Judgement: a diurnal corvid; not explicitly stated but consistent with daytime foraging, courtship and roosting behaviour described throughout the source.

traits.defense.note: Judgement: no explicit statement; magpies are described giving loud alarm chatter, and 'they organise themselves into gangs and use complex strategies to hunt other birds and fend off potential predators', but the shared behaviour program's default response to a close threat is to flee, so Defense was authored as Flee rather than Mob/Fight (the schema currently favours a single enum).

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: magpies are common in gardens and suburbs and breed at high densities near people ('Exploiter' urban affinity), but are noted as intelligent and wary, using tools and gang strategies against predators; a moderately high wariness was authored, higher than the more confiding blackbird.

habitat.use.note: Judgement split between ground foraging and time in trees/perches; the source describes preference for 'open countryside with scattered trees' and frequent ground feeding on insects, carrion and scraps, plus tree-nesting and roosting, without giving a numeric split.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored: magpies roost communally in trees/tall vegetation, tagged as 'perch' shelter.

habitat.resources.note: Small vertebrates/eggs, invertebrates, carrion, mast (acorns, seasonally weighted to autumn) and seed/grain from the Feeding section; nest and perch/shelter tags from the Breeding and Roosting sections. Weights are judgement, not separately sourced percentages.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Distribution and habitat section: Swedish magpies exclusively associated with settlements, rarely more than a few hundred metres from a dwelling, high suburban breeding densities, frequent near city centres. flight_distance_m and light_max are judgement (not separately sourced numbers).

seasonal.strategy.note: 'Magpies are usually sedentary and tend to stay close to their nesting territories in winter', with only northernmost populations (Sweden, Finland, Russia) moving south in harsh weather -- treated as the exception rather than the rule, so ActiveYearRound was used rather than PartialMigration.

seasonal.phases.note: Mating/courtship display in spring, clutches typically laid in April in Europe (incubation 21-22 days, fledging ~27 days) for the breeding phase, year-round pair territoriality, and winter flocking/communal roosting with other species. Exact start/end day-of-month boundaries are judgement.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Egg, altricial juvenile (hatch naked and blind, eyes open 7-8 days, fledge at ~27 days, fed by parents for several more weeks) and adult; no sourced juvenile-plumage duration was found so duration_days/scale were left unset.

vocalizations.chatter.note: 'a choking chatter chac-chac or a repetitive chac-chac-chac-chac' from the Description section, used as both the perching-songbird program's song and alarm call slots since the source does not describe a separate song.

vocalizations.begging.note: 'they also make an acute Uik Uik call that resembles the barking of a small dog' -- attributed to young/begging context; season_months (April-June) aligned to the breeding phase as a judgement.

look.note: Head, neck, breast and vent glossy black with metallic green/violet sheen; belly and scapulars pure white; wings black glossed green/purple with white inner primaries; graduated tail black glossed green and reddish-purple, about a quarter to over half of body length. Palette approximates the iridescent blue-green/purple sheen with a dark blue-teal 'markings' colour on the tail and outer wing feathers, since the schema palette has no separate iridescent slot; proportions (long tail, medium build) are authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program; flee_m and wariness raised above the blackbird example to reflect the source's description of magpies as wary, intelligent birds; song/alarm both point at the single chatter call since no distinct song was described.
